cls: Highly selective vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR-1, -2, -3) inhibitor (kinase inhibitor)
pharm: Oral small-molecule kinase inhibitor highly selective for VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3; blocks VEGF-driven angiogenesis in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer
quick: 5 mg orally once daily for 21 days then 7 days off, in 28-day cycles
With or without food at about the same time daily; swallow whole
Can cause fetal harm; effective contraception during and for 2 weeks after last dose
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose
No clinically significant PK difference in mild to severe impairment (CLcr 15-89)
Mild: no adjustment; moderate: not sufficiently studied; severe: not recommended
No specific interaction; limit use during therapy
Blood pressure, urine protein, LFTs, bleeding, infection, wound healing, PRES symptoms
summary: Fruquintinib (Fruzaqla) is a highly selective oral VEGFR-1, -2, and -3 inhibitor for adults with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and, if RAS wild-type and medically appropriate, an anti-EGFR therapy (FRESCO-2/FRESCO). The dose is 5 mg once daily for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle, with reductions to 4 mg then 3 mg for toxicity. Key risks are hypertension (including crisis), serious and fatal hemorrhage, GI perforation and fistula, hepatotoxicity, proteinuria with nephrotic syndrome, hand-foot skin reaction, PRES, arterial thromboembolism, impaired wound healing, and embryo-fetal toxicity. There are no absolute contraindications in labeling and no boxed warning.
indications: Treatment of adults with metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and, if RAS wild-type and medically appropriate, an anti-EGFR therapy

dosage.d: 5 mg once daily for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle, then 7 days off
dosage.t: Once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Swallow whole with or without food at about the same time daily; 1 mg and 5 mg capsules available

dosage.d: 4 mg once daily on the 21-on/7-off schedule
dosage.n: Withhold first for qualifying toxicities (e.g., persistent Grade 3 hypertension, proteinuria >=2 g/24 h); resume at lower dose on recovery

dosage.d: 3 mg once daily on the 21-on/7-off schedule
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue if 3 mg daily is not tolerated

dosage.d: Take a missed dose if <12 hours since the scheduled time; otherwise skip
dosage.n: Do not take two doses in one day; do not redose after vomiting, resume next scheduled dose

admin: Take at about the same time daily, with or without food; swallow capsules whole
Control blood pressure before starting; monitor weekly the first month, then at least monthly
Withhold during active infection; do not start with active infection
Withhold >=2 weeks before major surgery; do not resume until >=2 weeks after surgery with adequate healing
Permanently discontinue for GI perforation or fistula, nephrotic syndrome, arterial thromboembolism, or confirmed PRES
moa: Fruquintinib is a small-molecule kinase inhibitor highly selective for vascular endothelial growth factor receptors VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3. By blocking VEGF-driven signaling it inhibits endothelial proliferation and tumor angiogenesis, slowing growth of colorectal tumors. A mean QTc increase >20 ms was not observed at the recommended dose.

relative: Uncontrolled hypertension (do not initiate until controlled)
Bleeding risk or severe hemorrhage; recent arterial thromboembolism (initiation needs careful consideration)
Planned major surgery or unhealed wound
Aspirin or tartrazine sensitivity (1 mg capsules contain FD&C Yellow No. 5 and No. 6)
monitor: Bleeding signs; INR in anticoagulated patients
Urine protein, LFTs, infection signs, wound healing
Neurologic symptoms suggesting PRES (seizure, headache, visual change, confusion)

preg: Based on animal findings and mechanism, fruquintinib can cause fetal harm. In rats dosed during organogenesis, teratogenicity and embryo lethality occurred at exposures below the clinical exposure. There are no human pregnancy data. Advise pregnant women of fetal risk. Advise females of childbearing potential and males with female partners of childbearing potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose. Verify pregnancy status before starting.
lact: There are no data on fruquintinib in human milk or its effects on the child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose.
renal: No clinically significant PK differences were seen across mild to severe renal impairment (CLcr 15 to 89 mL/min); no dose adjustment is specified. Monitor proteinuria and blood pressure regardless of baseline function.
hepatic: No adjustment for mild hepatic impairment (TB <=ULN with AST >ULN, or TB >1 to 1.5 x ULN with any AST). Not sufficiently studied in moderate impairment (TB >1.5 to <3 x ULN); not recommended in severe impairment (TB >3 x ULN). Monitor liver tests before and during treatment; withhold, reduce, or stop for hepatotoxicity.

major: Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin: Cmax -12%, AUC -65%) - avoid; reduced efficacy expected
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inducers (e.g., efavirenz: predicted AUC -32%) - avoid if possible; continue same dose if co-use is unavoidable
minor: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (itraconazole), PPIs (rabeprazole): no clinically significant PK change; P-gp substrate (dabigatran) and BCRP substrate (rosuvastatin): no clinically significant change with fruquintinib
interactions.food: Take with or without food; no clinically significant food effect
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; limit alcohol during cancer therapy
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor blood pressure, urine protein (hold for >=2 g/24 h; stop for nephrotic syndrome), ALT/AST and bilirubin, CBC/bleeding signs, and INR with anticoagulants

serious: Hypertension including Grade 3-4 (19%) and hypertensive crisis
Serious and fatal hemorrhagic events including GI hemorrhage
GI perforation (Grade >=3 in 1.3%, one fatal) and fistula
Hepatotoxicity including Grade >=3 ALT/AST (5%) and fatal events (0.2%)
rare: Fatal hemorrhage or fatal hepatic failure
emergency: Hypertensive crisis signs (severe headache, chest pain, vision change, confusion)
Severe or persistent bleeding, black stools, or vomiting blood
Severe abdominal pain with fever (possible perforation)
Seizure, sudden vision loss, or confusion (possible PRES)

monitoring: Blood pressure weekly for the first month, then at least monthly and as indicated
Urine protein before and periodically; LFTs before and periodically
Bleeding signs; INR in patients on anticoagulants
Infection signs; wound healing around surgery (hold >=2 weeks before and after major surgery)
Neurologic exam and MRI if PRES suspected; discontinue if confirmed
counsel: Take 5 mg daily for 21 days then 7 days off each 28-day cycle, with or without food at the same time; swallow whole
Check blood pressure as directed and report severe headache, chest pain, vision changes, or confusion
Report any bleeding, black stools, coughing or vomiting blood, severe belly pain, fever, mouth or skin sores, or hand-foot redness and peeling
Tell surgeons and dentists you take this drug; it must be stopped at least 2 weeks before major surgery and healing must be complete before restarting
Use effective birth control during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose (both partners as applicable); do not breastfeed during and for 2 weeks after
pk: Anti-angiogenic effect accrues over weeks; steady state reached after about 14 days with ~4-fold accumulation
Geometric mean steady-state Cmax about 300 ng/mL; steady-state AUC0-24h about 5880 ng*h/mL; ~95% protein bound
Mean elimination half-life about 42 hours; apparent clearance about 14.8 mL/min
21 days on / 7 days off per 28-day cycle until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); brief exposure 15-30 C permitted per USP controlled room temperature
pearls: Selective VEGFR-1/2/3 blockade for refractory mCRC after fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, anti-VEGF, and anti-EGFR if RAS wild-type (FRESCO-2)
Hypertension in 49% with median onset 14 days: control BP first, then weekly checks the first month
Bleeding, perforation/fistula, and arterial clots can be fatal: permanent discontinuation rules are strict
Proteinuria median onset 22 days: hold for >=2 g/24 h, stop for nephrotic syndrome
Strong CYP3A inducers slash exposure (AUC -65%): avoid; 1 mg capsules contain tartrazine/sunset yellow dyes
missed: Take a missed dose if less than 12 hours have passed since the scheduled time. If more than 12 hours have passed, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take two doses on the same day. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take another dose; continue with the next scheduled dose.
overdose: No specific antidote for fruquintinib overdose is described. Manage with supportive care and monitoring for exaggerated effects such as severe hypertension, hemorrhage, proteinuria, skin toxicity, and hepatic injury, including blood pressure, bleeding signs, urine protein, and LFTs. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
